Hi Emily,

Thanks for the context and the sample file 0attached1. I took a quick pass and can definitely put together a conservative sizing sketch, but to make it actionable we need a few clarifications. I’ve attached a short intake spreadsheet (dedicated-sizing-form.xlsx) with the fields below; filling as many as you have available will speed things up:

Required / high-impact items:
- Typical and peak concurrent sessions (p50 / p95 / peak)
- Average prompt tokens and average model response tokens (p50 / p95)
- Distribution of short vs long responses (e.g., % responses > 512 tokens)
- Expected steady-state RPS and expected peak RPS (per minute and 5-minute rolling)
- Session duration and whether you use session affinity (sticky KV cache)
- KV-cache hit rate expectations or whether context is always re-sent per request
- Target latency SLO (p50/p95/p99) and whether p99 must be < 400ms or if p95 is the primary target
- Any hard constraints on model family (e.g., must use Llama2-70B, or open to quantized options)

Optional but helpful:
- Percent of requests that use tool calls / external API enrichments
- Burst characteristics (do you expect sustained bursts > 10 minutes?)
- Cost guardrails or preferred GPU SKUs

Next steps I propose: you fill the sheet and send back the sample telemetry; if easier we can take 30 minutes to go over telemetry together and I’ll produce a 1-page sizing sketch and a recommended SKU mix for Dedicated.

Timeline: once we have the filled form + a short token sample, I can deliver a preliminary sizing note within 48 hours (to share internally with capacity planning). Lead times for reservation depend on SKU and region, typically 4	6 weeks; we can recommend a conservative commit that supports your Q1 launch while keeping a small burst buffer.

Looping Marissa for capacity cost oversight and Karthik for sizing assumptions.

Best,

Thanks 0reated the intake sheet and attached a slightly enlarged token sample (integration_sample_tokens.csv) with anonymized fields. Answers inline below (quick notes):

- Typical concurrency (p50): 35 sessions
- Concurrency (p95): 120 sessions
- Peak concurrency (instant): 320 sessions for ~3 minutes during campaigns

- Avg prompt tokens: 140
- Avg response tokens: 560
- Response token distribution: p50=420, p95=1,200, ~12% > 1,024 tokens

- Steady-state RPS (global): 55 req/s
- 5-minute peak RPS: 480 req/s (during campaign spikes)

- Session duration: avg 2.5 minutes (many short flows), we do session affinity for a subset (~60%) using a simple KV store for embeddings and partial context. Cache hit estimated at 45% on average.

- Tooling: ~8% of requests call external APIs for enrichment (adds ~80-120ms on average)

- Model preference: open to Llama2-70B-like / 4-bit quantized where quality is acceptable. Primary constraint is p95 latency < 400ms for interactive workflows; offline summarization can be relaxed.

Timeline: we intend to close a committed capacity conversation by late December and ramp in January. Willing to commit to a 12-month reserved pool if the economics match our growth expectations.

Appreciate a conservative sketch and any obvious pitfalls you see.

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Forwarding VoxCraft’s filled intake and token sample (see thread below). Quick read:
- Workload mix is ~60% interactive (p95 latency target < 400ms), 40% longer offline summarization.
- Token mix is heavy on responses (avg response ~560 tokens), p95 ~1.2k and ~12% >1k which increases tail GPU time significantly.
- They have decent KV cache behavior (45% effective hit) with session affinity for ~60% of sessions 0 good for us.
- Peak instantaneous concurrency of 320 for ~3 minutes and 5-min peak RPS ~480 are the main burst drivers.

Prelim capacity sketch (ridiculously conservative, pre-optimization):
- If we target interactive p95 < 400ms using a Llama2-70B-class baseline (quantized): assume ~1.8x token-cost vs smaller 30B variants due to KV working set + attention costs.
- Estimated committed pool: 6 x 80GB-class GPUs (A100-80GB equivalents) as baseline to cover sustained peak concurrency and 5-min burst when combined with aggressive batching and KV cache.
- Add 2x buffer GPUs for short-term bursts (can be on burst pool / cheaper GPU type) OR we can route overflow to hosted pool with graceful fallbacks.
- If they accept a 30B quantized model for interactive paths we can likely reduce to 4 x 80GB-class equivalents.

Risk/assumptions that affect final number:
- Fraction of >1k responses stays at 12% (if this doubles, GPU minutes spike significantly)
- External API enrichment adds latency and reduces effective GPU throughput for pipeline edges
- Their target p95 < 400ms is aggressive for 70B-class models at ~1.2k token p95 without aggressive KV caching and batching gains

Ask: can you both sanity-check the ballpark and transform into a short SKU-level recommendation we can include in a Q4 commitment proposal? Marissa, please flag pricing bands and whether we should propose burst routing to hosted as part of the commercial package. I’ll schedule a 30-minute sizing walkthrough with VoxCraft next week (will include our preliminary note).

Thanks,
Irene
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
